current_focus.summary: Owner confirmed Cycle 1 Charter & Scope (D1-D6): standalone EmDash plugin with optional Commerce/Ship/Payments adapters + standalone open-source US County/State sales-tax schedule package; multi-processor clearing (Stripe net payouts + Authorize.Net gross batches + future providers) & free CSV/OFX + /yr user-direct SimpleFIN; simple Cash | Accrual toggle (defer Inventory sync); Safe-to-Spend 3-bucket header + processor-independent SST/Census county sales-tax workbooks + quarterly income-tax pacer with CPA-first handoff default; built-in Gusto payroll bridge + free native 1099 tracking (reject native W-2 withholding); and human-gated locks/CPA handoffs alongside agent staging.

decisions.question: Where does @dinkuskit/books run and store ledger data?
decisions.rationale: Expands adoption to every EmDash site (not just storefronts), turns open county sales-tax schedules into a standalone OSS builder/agent resource, and prevents data lock-in.

decisions.choice: Free CSV/OFX/QFX statement imports + direct read-only processor/bank keys + optional /yr user-owned SimpleFIN Bridge token (zsh vendor billing/markup) feeding a dual-balance (Statement vs Ledger) reconciliation engine (zsh.00-diff lock + non-destructive Remove & Redo) and multi-processor settlement clearing supporting both net-fee payouts (Stripe payout_id) and gross batch settlements + separate acquirer fee debits (Authorize.Net batchId and future @dinkuskit/payments providers).

history.choice: CSV/OFX/QFX statement import + optional /yr user-owned SimpleFIN Bridge & native read-only Stripe/Mercury APIs into a strict dual-balance (Statement vs Ledger) reconciliation engine (zsh.00-diff Blank->C->R tie-out + clearing accounts + non-destructive Remove & Redo)

decisions.question: How does @dinkuskit/books ingest bank/card lines and reconcile statements?
decisions.rationale: Replaces Xero reconciliation across checking, credit cards, standard gateways, and high-risk gateways without enterprise Plaid proxy minimums or Stripe-only lock-in.

decisions.choice: Dual-date append-only ledger (transaction date + settled date) powering a 1-click Cash | Accrual toggle on P&L and Balance Sheet reports; treat inventory buys as standard categorized purchases in V1 and defer live @dinkuskit/inventory SKU COGS sync to a post-V1 cycle.

history.choice: Single append-only journal core projecting both Accrual and Cash basis (1099-K Constructive-Receipt Cash default + Bank-Deposit Cash filter), with Purchase-Based and Sales-Based COGS fed by @dinkuskit/inventory movements + pre-cutover double-deduction guard (defer full multi-layer FIFO POs)

decisions.question: How does @dinkuskit/books model Cash vs Accrual reporting and inventory COGS?
decisions.rationale: Delivers Xero-equivalent Cash/Accrual P&L and CPA tie-outs cleanly without premature cross-plugin inventory complexity.

decisions.choice: Leave checkout tax rate calculation outside Books; own post-checkout tax readiness across three pieces: (1) Three-Bucket 'Safe to Spend' cash header (Sales Tax Owed | Income Tax Set-Aside | Safe to Spend), (2) Processor-independent US County & Local District resolution (via free official SST boundary/rate CSVs, US Census batch geocoder, and state DOR GIS packs—working identically for Stripe, Authorize.Net, and CSV imports) producing CPA-ready monthly .xlsx/.csv County Sales Tax Workbooks, and (3) Rolling quarterly Federal + State income-tax set-aside pacer (Apr 15 / Jun 15 / Sep 15 / Jan 15). Default output is CPA-first handoff (with optional self-filing from the same verified workbook); defer 50-state nexus threshold alarms and resale-certificate vaults beyond V1.

decisions.rationale: Eliminates monthly county sales-tax spreadsheet pain for zsh across any payment gateway, ends Q4 tax surprises, and keeps the merchant's CPA as the filing shield between the business and tax authorities.

decisions.question: How should @dinkuskit/books handle 1099 contractors vs W-2 payroll and Gusto?
decisions.rationale: Avoids IRC 6672 personal trust-fund liability and Gusto partner-API gates while making Gusto effortless on EmDash and saving 1099-only businesses /mo + /contractor.

decisions.choice: EmDash Admin UI, CLI, and read-default MCP share one typed domain service: agents ingest feeds/batches, stage bank matches, resolve county schedules, and assemble monthly/year-end CPA workbooks; human confirmation is strictly required for new vendor rules, owner/tax elections, statement reconciliation locks, period closes, and final CPA/external handoff.

history.choice: Shared typed service + read-default MCP: agents auto-ingest deterministic store/payout/postage events, OCR receipts/resale certs, and stage bank matches/exception drafts; human confirmation is required for new vendor rules, owner-draw / ,500 safe-harbor elections, statement reconciliation locks, period closes, and external tax/1099 filings

decisions.question: Where is the exact authority line between AI agents (CLI/MCP) and human operators (Admin UI)?
decisions.rationale: Preserves the DinkusKit human+agent side-by-side principle while keeping humans and CPAs in control of legal/tax sign-off.

alternatives: Cycle 2B: Standalone Open-Source US County & State Sales-Tax Schedule Package (SST + Census batch geocoder + CPA-ready .xlsx/.csv county workbooks)
recommendation.reason: Core ledger and statement reconciliation underpin P&L, Safe-to-Spend, Gusto clearing, and tax reserves—while the decoupled County Sales-Tax Schedule package has zero EmDash lock-in and can also be built immediately as an independent high-impact module.
recommendation.recommended: Cycle 2A: Core Double-Entry Ledger, Chart of Accounts & Bank/Multi-Processor Reconciliation Kernel (CSV/OFX + SimpleFIN + Stripe & Authorize.Net clearing)
